4. Safety instructions 
 
4.1. 
General 
 
NOTE: 
This chapter includes the safety instructions that must be complied with when operating 
or servicing the Z72 wind turbine. The contents of this chapter must be read carefully 
before attempting any work on or with the unit.

It is the owners’ responsibility to ensure that each person involved in the operation or 
maintenance of the turbine, has received the appropriate training or instructions and has 
thoroughly read and clearly understood the safety instructions in this chapter. 
 
 
4.1.1. Intended audience 
 
This User’s Guide is intended for the following two target groups: 
 
• 
Operators of the turbine 
• 
Maintenance personnel of the turbine

Maintenance personnel of the turbine 
 
This manual is not intended for commissioning staff. 
 
Operation: 
The operator is mainly responsible for the operation of the wind turbine (starting and 
stopping the turbine) using the Local Operator Panel mounted on the ABB Wind Power 
Converter. An operator is able to diagnose faults, and can decide if it is safe to reset 
faults and to restart the turbine. 
 
Maintenance: 
The maintenance personnel is mainly responsible for: 
 
• 
Periodical checks

into Service mode, use the service features of the control system, and how to restart the 
turbine after service. 
 
 
4.1.2. Required qualification 
 
Personnel must be fully trained and acquainted with the turbine and its control system. 
Operators of the turbine are not expected to have prior experience of wind turbines

expected to have prior experience of wind turbines. 
However, the operator must know how to operate the turbine and must understand the 
meaning of the events on the Local Operator Panel located on the converter door to 
decide on the appropriate actions to take.

5.2. 
Introduction 
 
 
 
 
Figure 1 The Z72 2MW variable speed wind turbine 
 
The Harakosan Z72/2000 wind turbine is a 3-bladed, direct drive, variable speed, pitch 
controlled wind turbine with a rotor diameter of 70.6 m and a nominal power rating of 
2000 kW. The turbine is designed for use in areas for which IEC wind class IIB applies. 
 
The Z72 turbine was designed with demanding offshore and remote ap

was designed with demanding offshore and remote application in mind, 
and has as few moving parts as possible.

Major advantages of the permanent magnet design are the lower generator losses and

5.3. 
Principle of operation 
 
A variable speed wind turbine adapts its rotor speed to speed of the wind. By matching 
the rotor speed to the speed of the wind, the conversion of wind energy to mechanical 
energy is optimal. This variable rotor speed also causes the frequency of the power 
generated by the generator to be variable and this power cannot be directly coupled to 
the grid. For this reason, a power conver

pled to 
the grid. For this reason, a power converter, or AC-DC-AC converter, first rectifies the 
variable frequency power to an intermediate DC power, and than inverts this DC power 
into AC power with the frequency of the grid. Advantage of this mechanism is that the 
inverter from DC power to AC power can control the reactive power between certain 
limits (optional), supporting the grid quality. 
 
Matching the speed of the rotor to the speed of the wind is done by controlling the power 
cou

of the wind is done by controlling the power 
coupled to the grid as a function of the actual rotor speed according to a so-called Pn 
curve. This Pn curve has a maximum at 2 MW: the maximum power of the wind turbine. 
Should the wind speed increase when the turbine is running at 2 MW, then the excess 
energy of the wind is diverted from the blades by pitching the blades to vane position. 
 
Each individual blade is controlled by means of an electrically actuated system consisting 
of a DC serv

of a DC servo motor. Emergency operation, essential when the coupling to the grid is lost 
or the normal pitch control is faulty, is achieved by fast positioning the blades to vane 
position by batteries. In case the overspeed protection system inside the PLC is not 
functioning, a backup system consisting of an external electrical overspeed switch will 
guarantee safe shutdown of the turbine.

causing the alarm is not corrected.
